children: ADARx Pharmaceuticals, a late-clinical stage biotechnology company focused on next‑generation siRNA therapeutics, filed for an initial public offering. The company plans to list on the Nasdaq Global Market under the ticker "ADRX." Proceeds will support multiple clinical programs, including complement-mediated diseases, hereditary angioedema, thrombotic disease, obesity and neurodegeneration.

ADARx Pharmaceuticals is a biotechnology company developing next‑generation small interfering RNA (siRNA) medicines designed for deep, durable, and selective gene silencing. The company’s proprietary MST (messenger RNA Silencing Technology) optimizes siRNA sequence and chemistry for potency and durability, while its CTD (Cell Targeted Delivery) platform enables targeted delivery to hepatic and extrahepatic tissues, including adipose and neurons. ADARx’s wholly owned pipeline includes three clinical programs—agazisiran (CFB) for complement‑mediated diseases, onvuzosiran (PKK) for hereditary angioedema with FDA Fast Track and orphan designation, and ADX‑626 (FXI) for secondary stroke prevention—and two advanced preclinical programs: ADX‑077 for obesity and ADX‑199 targeting APP in neurons for neurodegenerative diseases.

The company has demonstrated program‑to‑program clinical consistency with potent and durable target knockdown, supporting infrequent dosing intervals (e.g., quarterly to semi‑annual). Beyond its core programs, ADARx is expanding into additional tissues such as microglia, skeletal muscle, cardiac muscle and ocular tissues, and is advancing bispecific-siRNA designs. A discovery‑stage collaboration with AbbVie adds non‑dilutive capital and validation to its platform, positioning ADARx to scale pipeline development across multiple therapeutic areas.
